notes:
Access: same as Bestsellers pass - /shop/* blocked by Akamai 403 at tier 1 (curl_cffi) and tier 2 (headless Playwright); reached via Claude-in-Chrome (tier 3, real Chrome). robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow.

Sale-vs-Clearance reasoning (the brief's critical test): Pottery Barn's top nav 'Sale' tab lands on /shop/sale/exclusive-savings/, titled 'Shop All Deals', header 'Labor Day Sale: Up To 70% Off' (6836 items) - this is a generic, clearly temporary promotional campaign page (named for a calendar holiday sale event) and was correctly EXCLUDED as Clearance per the brief. However, that same 'Sale' section's own sub-nav exposes a distinct 'Clearance' entry that is NOT just a filter label - it is its own dedicated category page at /shop/sale/all-clearance/ (redirects to /shop/sale/shop-all-clearance/?cm_src=OLDLINK) with its own breadcrumb 'Sale > Clearance', its own SEO title 'Clearance Furniture & Home Décor | Pottery Barn', and its own on-page copy ('Our clearance selection offers timeless pieces at exceptional value... Clearance shopping is the perfect way to experiment with new looks'). This satisfies the brief's test (site's own taxonomy clearly treats it as Clearance) and was included as the primary/canonical row.

A second, separate 'Clearance' link was also found inside the generic Sale/Deals page's own left-nav (labelled 'Clearance (1478)' as a productpricetype=sale filter facet, landing on /shop/sale/clearance+exclusive-savings/productpricetype-m-sale-ff0010151c-1/, page title 'Clearance All Sale', header 'Clearance All Sale — View 1478 Items'). This is a different, smaller count (1478 vs. the canonical page's 2119), so per brief guidance ('different counts -> keep both, do not blindly dedupe') it is recorded as a second row, but flagged MANUAL REVIEW since it lives inside the temporary Labor Day Sale campaign page rather than being its own clean top-level category, so it's unclear whether it's a genuinely separate merchandising listing or a differently-scoped cut of the same clearance tag.

Other navigation checked: main nav, footer, site search not needed since the real Sale/Clearance nav hierarchy was directly walked. No other Clearance/Outlet/Final Sale/Last Chance wording found anywhere else on the site (Furniture/Lighting/etc. category pages carry only generic 'Sale'/'Limited Time Offer' product badges, not standalone Clearance PLPs).

It reports a different item count (1478) than the canonical /shop/sale/all-clearance/ page (2119), so it may be a genuinely distinct, promo-scoped clearance cut, or a differently-filtered view of overlapping inventory.
